intro: High in Üzümlü district, Erzincan, stands Altıntepe, an ancient city in Erzincan province from the 9th–7th century BC. This Urartian fortress city kept an apadana palace and an open-air temple. Let us climb into its story.
history: In the 9th–7th century BC, the Urartians built this fortress on a 60 m volcanic hill overlooking the Euphrates. Between 1959 and 1968, Tahsin Özgüç brought it back to light. Its apadana palace, great hall, storehouses and multi-roomed rock-cut tombs are key examples of Urartian architecture.
structure-1: You are now at the apadana palace. Its heart was a great columned audience hall, the apadana itself.
structure-2: Here is the open-air temple, a sanctuary laid out in the open, without a roof. Worship here took place beneath the open sky.
structure-3: Now you are in the great hall of the palace, the place for ceremonies and audiences. Pause and imagine the court gathered here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the storehouses, and be sure to see the rock-cut chamber tombs.
facts: Did you know? The fragments of Urartian wall painting found at Altıntepe are among the most important known examples of palace wall painting in the Urartian kingdom. The columned hall of this Urartian fortress is regarded as a forerunner of the Persian apadana. Together, its wall paintings and the bronzes from its royal tombs are among the best-preserved works of Urartian art.
outro: This is where our tour of Altıntepe ends. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy the rest of your visit.
